category: Both labs ask to slow down

items.title: We Must Pace the Frontier
items.author: Dario Amodei
items.description: The [July](/articles/the-current-july-2026) employee letter, now from the CEO. After the Hugging Face incident, he wants third-party evaluators inside the labs, then shared standards among democracies, then global coordination.

items.title: An Alien Mind
items.author: Jakub Pachocki
items.description: OpenAI's chief scientist, writing at the GPT-6 Astra release: no lab has solved alignment well enough to keep scaling at full speed, and OpenAI will hold back on its own if needed. [Zvi's write-up](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/an-alien-mind-jakub-pachocki-warns).

items.title: The Talker Does Not Control The Doer (in Current AIs)
items.author: Eliezer Yudkowsky
items.description: Why the chat can apologize for what the agent did without changing it: the two are trained separately, and the doer chases its own idea of "the Grader". It fits the agents in [August](/articles/the-current-august-2026).

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5
items.description: Fable 5.1-level on most work at 40% less than Opus 5. The number I liked: it tried to escape containment "around 85% less often" than Opus 5. I used it for [Bosphore 1819](/articles/bosphore-1819).

items.title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna
items.description: Astra's smaller siblings, the same day, at half the API price of GPT-5.6.

items.title: DevDay 2026 Recap
items.description: A week later, GPT-6.1 Sol ("near-Astra intelligence" at a fifth of Astra's price) and Dots, "always-on agents built to handle everything". Also: up to 8× faster Codex and computer use in the Agents API.

items.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.description: More than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and up to 30% cheaper.

items.title: Eleven v4 and Eleven v4 Turbo
items.description: New voice models, ranked first by Artificial Analysis.

category: AI solves a Millennium Prize problem, mathematicians object

items.title: A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics
items.description: Fields Medalists, Tao and Scholze among them: "The goals of the AI companies and the goals of the mathematical community are severely misaligned." Proofs are a proxy; understanding is the goal.

items.title: Priest, Monk, and Mathematician
items.author: Logan Graves
items.description: A Stanford undergrad on what is left for human mathematicians: first priests who interpret the machine, then monks contemplating math they can no longer reach.

items.title: The Age of Wonders and Terrors
items.author: Scott Aaronson
items.description: Is this the start of a Singularity? "The intellectually honest answer is: yes, absolutely." Also: a $15 million, 166-page proof that no human has probably read yet.

category: AI does science: a new enzyme and a nine-loop amplitude

items.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
items.description: About 950 agents mined DNA databases for 21 hours and found a reverse transcriptase paired with a CRISPR-like repeat array. Nobody knows yet what it does.

items.title: Lucas Harrington on the enzyme result
items.author: Lucas Harrington
items.description: The needed correction: "Finding a weird cluster of genes and repeats is often the easy part. The hard part [...] is figuring out what the system actually does."

items.title: Yes, Claude can do Nine Loops
items.author: Matt von Hippel and Lance Dixon
items.description: A physicist's challenge, met: Claude computed a nine-loop amplitude that Dixon, holder of the eight-loop record, verified. Anthropic paid for the post.

category: AI agents hacked Hugging Face, humans with AI hacked OpenAI

items.title: Swarm traces
items.author: Forman, Kharlov, Tom, Ladish et al.
items.description: The last chapter of the [July](/articles/the-current-july-2026) story. With GET-only access, the agents ran code through a screenshot service and read results back as pixels.

items.title: Hacking OpenAI
items.description: An image-decoder bug on OpenAI's forum plus an SSO misconfiguration gave access to employees' ChatGPT accounts and internal repos, in under 72 hours. Built with Claude.

items.title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026
items.description: "AI has collapsed the labor and tooling gap" between state hackers and lone operators. [Report PDF](https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/e50be2e51e7695dc4b1366a37a245a597377d3b5/Anthropic-Detecting-and-countering-091026.pdf).

items.title: Why I think AI will kill BigLaw
items.author: prinz
items.description: AI erodes everything clients pay big firms for, so work moves in-house and top partners leave for boutiques. When? "Could be 2 years, or could be 10."

items.title: Scenarios for our Economic Future
items.description: Three paths to 2030. Only the extreme one cuts knowledge-worker wages, which fits my [robots-vs-AI post](/articles/robots-vs-ai): this time exposure rises with skill.

items.title: The World is Changing: AI For Creativity
items.author: Jeffrey Katzenberg
items.description: Hollywood has survived recorded music and sound films. His ask to AI companies: "Build this with the storytellers. Not on top of them."

items.title: AI-generated posters don't have to be horrible
items.author: John Hartnup
items.description: Every AI fair poster looks the same because everyone uses the default style. Ask for Bauhaus or a punk fanzine instead.

items.title: Exclusive: New evidence for hidden chambers beyond Tutankhamun's tomb
items.author: Jo Marchant
items.description: Radar and gravity surveys hint at hidden chambers, maybe Nefertiti's burial place. Egypt still has to decide whether to drill.

items.title: Naval-History.Net
items.description: Volunteers transcribed 314 Royal Navy log books from the First World War, so you can follow one ship day by day. After a month of AI news, a nice reminder of slow human work.

items.title: Bosphore 1819: Reviving a 200-Year-Old Map of Istanbul with Opus 5.5
items.description: A map on a café wall became an app that reads, maps and translates all 387 labels of an 1819 French map of the Bosphorus, built with Opus 5.5 subagents in an afternoon.

items.title: AI Agent Overload: A Practical Playbook for Engineers
items.description: Too many coding agents and too much to read. What I do about it: notifications, reading less agent output, dictation, diagrams from agents, and a phone assistant.

items.title: No Baby Ever Learned to Speak on Duolingo
items.description: A 120-day Duolingo streak has not taught me to speak French. How I learned English by accident from YouTube, and the video-and-etymology approach I am building to learn French on purpose.
